terms.definition: AWS's native monitoring and observability service that collects metrics, logs, alarms, and events from virtually all AWS services
terms.example: Like a hospital patient monitor — tracking vitals of your cloud infrastructure in real time

terms.definition: Numerical data points collected over time that track the performance and health of AWS resources
terms.example: CPU utilization percentage, network bytes in/out, request latency in milliseconds

terms.definition: Text-based records of events from applications and AWS services, organized into Log Groups and Log Streams
terms.example: Application error messages, HTTP request/response records, keep-alive health checks

terms.definition: A container in CloudWatch Logs that holds all log streams from a particular application or AWS service
terms.example: All logs from your SageMaker pizza-classifier endpoint would be in one Log Group

terms.definition: A sequence of log events from a specific source within a Log Group, such as one EC2 instance or one model variant
terms.example: Logs from model-variant-A vs model-variant-B in the same Log Group would be separate Log Streams

terms.definition: An interactive query tool within CloudWatch that lets you search, filter, and analyze log data using a SQL-like query language
terms.example: Running 'filter @message like /500/' to find all server errors in the last hour

terms.definition: An AI-powered feature in CloudWatch Log Insights that analyzes query results and provides a plain-English summary of patterns, anomalies, and potential issues — launched globally August 2024
terms.example: Summarizing 717 log entries and discovering that 3 were Service Unavailable errors at specific timestamps

terms.definition: A number counting seconds or milliseconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC, used universally in log systems for precise event timing
terms.example: The timestamp 1711269540000 represents March 24, 2024 at approximately 08:39:00 UTC (in milliseconds)

terms.definition: The universal time standard used by CloudWatch and most logging systems; users must manually convert to local time for analysis
terms.example: An error logged at 15:39 UTC equals 08:39 AM Pacific Time (UTC-7)

terms.definition: HTTP status code indicating a successful request — the server received, understood, and processed the request
terms.example: A successful model invocation returns 200, meaning the AI received your image and returned a classification

terms.definition: HTTP status code family indicating a server-side error — the service encountered a problem processing the request
terms.example: Getting a 500 error during a regional outage means the AI service backend is unavailable, not that your request was wrong

terms.definition: AWS service that records all API calls made in your account, capturing who did what, when, and from where — used for audit and compliance
terms.example: CloudTrail would show you that a security group was modified by a specific IAM user at a specific time

terms.definition: A load-balancing mechanism in Amazon Bedrock that distributes AI model requests across multiple endpoints; required for large models like Claude Sonnet
terms.example: A US regional inference profile routes Claude requests between Oregon and Virginia data centers for load balancing

terms.definition: A Bedrock inference profile that routes requests to the best-available model endpoint worldwide, providing maximum reach but exposure to any regional outage
terms.example: During Middle East infrastructure outages, global profiles experienced severe timeouts as the routing system was overwhelmed

terms.definition: A Bedrock inference profile that limits request routing to data centers within a specific geography (US, EU, etc.), providing isolation from other regional issues
terms.example: Switching from global to US regional profile stopped timeout errors caused by Middle East infrastructure problems

terms.definition: Periodic health check requests sent to a running service to confirm it is still operational; these constitute the majority of log entries for always-on endpoints
terms.example: A SageMaker endpoint receives a keep-alive GET request every 30 seconds, generating hundreds of 200 OK log entries per hour

terms.definition: The time delay between sending a request and receiving a response; a key metric for monitoring application performance
terms.example: Normal AI app latency is 5 seconds; latency of 45 seconds or more indicates a serious problem

terms.definition: The SQL-like query language used in CloudWatch Log Insights with commands like fields, filter, stats, sort, and limit
terms.example: 'fields @timestamp, @message | filter @message like /error/ | sort @timestamp desc | limit 100'

terms.definition: A public web page showing the current operational status of all AWS services across all regions; first stop for investigating suspected infrastructure issues
terms.example: During the March 2025 Middle East disruption, the health dashboard showed affected services and regions

terms.definition: An account-specific dashboard in AWS that shows incidents affecting your particular resources and account, with proactive notifications
terms.example: Unlike the public dashboard, this shows specifically that your EC2 instance in ap-south-1 is affected by the current event

terms.definition: A deployed AI model accessible via HTTP — essentially a web API that accepts requests (like images) and returns predictions
terms.example: The pizza/not-pizza classifier was deployed as a SageMaker endpoint that returned JSON with confidence scores

terms.definition: A specific deployment configuration of a model within a SageMaker endpoint, allowing A/B testing of different model versions simultaneously
terms.example: You might have variant-A using your v1 model and variant-B using your v2 model, both in the same endpoint

terms.definition: An error returned by an AWS service when the request format is incorrect or doesn't meet the service's requirements
terms.example: Invoking Claude Sonnet directly by model ID instead of using an inference profile returns a Validation Exception
